stem: The diagram shows Vedika's four-sided card, tilted on the page. Opposite sides are $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $3\,\mathrm{cm}$, and every corner is $90^\circ$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly names the figure?

options.text: A rectangle, because opposite sides are equal and all angles are $90^\circ$, even though the card is tilted.
A square, because any four-sided shape with right angles is called a square.
A rectangle, because the opposite sides are equal.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Opposite sides are equal and all angles are $90^\circ$, but the sides are not all equal, so the figure is a rectangle and not a square; tilting does not change lengths or angles.

teacher.key_rationale: 5 cm and 3 cm opposite sides with four right angles make a rectangle, not a square. Calling every right-angled quadrilateral a square swaps the label. Citing only opposite sides equal omits the right-angle condition needed in the full check.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as a tilted 5 cm by 3 cm rectangle.
